headline: Matt Mullenweg reportedly back as Automattic CEO after brief ouster
summary: Automattic founder Matt Mullenweg claims he's back in control of the company, just two days after being placed on paid leave.
details: Automattic founder Matt Mullenweg has reportedly been reinstated as CEO, just two days after being placed on a paid leave of absence. Mullenweg allegedly informed staff that CFO Mark Davies conspired with the board to remove him, but has since stated the board is "back in agreement" and he is "in control of Automattic."

The situation unfolded rapidly, with reports indicating that Davies was initially appointed interim CEO. However, Mullenweg's messages suggest a swift resolution, with Davies' Slack account reportedly deactivated and all admins removed from the company's Slack.

Mullenweg, who leads Automattic, the company behind WordPress.com, Tumblr, and Beeper, made light of the situation on X, posting "If you don’t have a coup attempt every few years, you’re not hiring strong enough leaders," adding that this was his fifth such "attempt."

While an Automattic spokesperson initially confirmed Mullenweg was "currently on leave" and Davies' interim appointment, the company has not yet provided a further statement following Mullenweg's claims of reinstatement.
